segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I ask, then: has God rejected his people? Absolutely not! For I too am an Israelite, a descendant of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: God has not rejected his people, whom he foreknew. Or do you not know what the scripture says in the passage about Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Lord, they have killed your prophets, they have torn down your altars; I alone am left, and they are seeking my life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But what does the divine reply say to him?

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “I have kept for myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So in the same way, at the present time too, there has come to be a remnant by a choice of grace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And if it is by grace, it is no longer on the basis of works; otherwise grace would no longer be grace.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What then? What Israel is seeking, it did not obtain. The chosen obtained it, but the rest were hardened,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes that would not see and ears that would not hear, to this very day.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And David says:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Let their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution for them;

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and keep their backs bent always.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I ask, then: did they stumble so as to fall? Absolutely not! Rather, by their misstep salvation has come to the Gentiles, to make Israel jealous.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now if their misstep means riches for the world, and their defeat riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness mean!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now I am speaking to you Gentiles. Inasmuch, then, as I am an apostle to the Gentiles, I honor my ministry,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: in the hope that I may somehow make my own flesh and blood jealous and save some of them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if their being cast aside means reconciliation for the world, what will their being taken back mean, if not life from the dead?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: If the firstfruits are holy, so is the whole batch of dough; and if the root is holy, so are the branches.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, though a wild olive, were grafted in among them and came to share in the rich root of the olive tree,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: do not boast over the branches. If you do boast, it is not you who carry the root, but the root that carries you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You will say, then,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: True enough: they were broken off for lack of faith, and you stand by faith. Do not think highly of yourself, but be afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Consider, then, the kindness and the severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but God's kindness toward you, if you continue in his kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they too, if they do not continue in their lack of faith, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For if you were cut out of what is by nature a wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these, the natural branches, be grafted into their own olive tree!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For I do not want you to be unaware of this mystery, brothers and sisters, so that you will not be wise in your own eyes: a hardening has come upon Israel in part, until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and in this way all Israel will be saved, as it is written:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “The deliverer will come from Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As regards the good news, they are enemies for your sake; but as regards the choice, they are beloved for the sake of the forefathers.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For just as you were once disobedient to God but have now been shown mercy through their disobedience,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so they too have now been disobedient, so that by the mercy shown to you they too may now be shown mercy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For God has confined all in disobedience so that he may show mercy to all.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: O the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and how untraceable his ways!

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?”

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Or who has given to him first, that he should be repaid?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be the glory forever. Amen.

notes.note: The Greek says simply ‘in Elijah’. Before chapter and verse numbers existed, a section of Scripture was commonly cited by its subject. The passage is 1 Kings 19:10–18.

The Greek noun is the ordinary word for a selection or choice. ‘Election’ is the traditional rendering and remains standard in theological writing, but in modern English it suggests voting. In verse 7 the same word is used concretely for the people chosen (‘the chosen’), and it returns in verse 28.

notes.phrase: otherwise grace would no longer be grace
notes.note: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add: ‘But if it is by works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work.’ Most of the earliest witnesses lack the sentence, and most scholars regard it as a later expansion. SBLGNT omits it.

The Greek word means ‘nations’ or ‘peoples’. In the plural, in Jewish usage, it is the regular term for the non-Jewish peoples. This translation renders it ‘Gentiles’ in that sense and ‘nations’ where peoples as such are meant; both represent one Greek word.

The word denotes a lapse or wrongdoing and is usually rendered ‘trespass’ or ‘transgression’. Paul sets it here beside ‘stumble’ and ‘fall’, and ‘misstep’ keeps both the moral sense and the image. It refers to Israel's failure to accept the good news, not to a trivial slip.

The word means what fills or completes something. Here and in verse 25 many interpreters take it numerically (‘their full number’, ‘full inclusion’), in contrast with the present remnant. Others take it as Israel's complete restoration. ‘Fullness’ leaves the question open, as the Greek does.

notes.traditional: their rejection / the casting away of them
notes.note: Most interpreters understand this as God's temporary setting aside of unbelieving Israel, matched by ‘their being taken back’. A minority read it as Israel's own rejection of the good news. The Greek word differs from the one for ‘rejected’ in verses 1–2, where Paul denies that God has rejected his people.

The image comes from Numbers 15:17–21, where the first portion of each batch of dough is offered to God. Paul's point is that the consecrated part marks the whole as God's. Whether the firstfruits and the root stand for the patriarchs or for the present remnant of Jewish believers is debated; most take the root to be the patriarchs.

Normal practice was to graft shoots from a cultivated olive onto wild stock, not the reverse. Paul's own phrase shows that he knows his picture runs against ordinary procedure. The point is that the inclusion of Gentiles is God's doing and not the natural course of things.

notes.phrase: and in this way all Israel will be saved
notes.traditional: and so all Israel shall be saved
notes.note: The Greek adverb normally expresses manner (‘in this way’) and not time (‘and then’), though some interpreters argue for a temporal sense. ‘All Israel’ is also disputed. Most scholars take it as the Jewish people as a whole, not necessarily every individual; others take it as the total of chosen Jews across history, and a minority as the whole people of God, Jew and Gentile together.

‘Gospel’ has become a religious term or a book title. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, used also of imperial proclamations. Many modern translations already alternate between ‘good news’ and ‘gospel’.

notes.phrase: by the mercy shown to you
notes.traditional: by the mercy shown to you
notes.note: In Greek this phrase stands before ‘so that’ and could be read with what precedes: ‘they have been disobedient for the sake of the mercy shown to you’. Most translators and commentators take it with what follows, as here, matching the structure of verse 30. Some manuscripts also lack the second ‘now’ in this verse.

candidates.reason: The plural address to mixed congregations recurs throughout the letters, and translators split between ‘brothers’, ‘brothers and sisters’ and ‘brethren’.
In period usage it means a secret now disclosed, which ‘mystery’ obscures for modern readers; ‘secret’ and ‘mystery’ should not alternate across the Pauline letters, Gospels and Revelation.
It recurs in Romans 4–5, Ephesians, Colossians and the Gospels as ‘trespass’, ‘transgression’ or ‘offence’, and one decision is needed on whether the image of a false step should show.
The noun and its verb recur across the Gospels and letters as ‘stumbling block’, ‘offence’, ‘trap’ or ‘cause of sin’, and readers would be misled by unexplained variation.
With ἐκλεκτός and ἐκλέγομαι it forms a word group where ‘election/elect’ and ‘choice/chosen’ compete, and it needs one decision across Romans, 1 Thessalonians and 2 Peter.

patch.reason: euangelion promoted to active after full-run drift (good news 37 / gospel 35)
